flaws.title: Says Paystream dedupes retried charges by orderId
flaws.reply:
Thanks for the quick look 🙏 On 1, tbh I'm pretty sure Paystream already dedupes on orderId, it's right there in the charge metadata, so a retry for the same order can't create a second charge. The header is just belt and braces for the clients. Not sure we need to thread the key through.

On 2, a declined card will just decline again, so retrying a 402 is harmless, it only costs a few hundred ms. But sure, I can narrow it to timeouts/429/5xx if you'd rather.

And yep, good catch on `log`, I'll pass it in. I'll add a failure-path test too.
flaws.wrong: Say retries are safe because Paystream already dedupes charges on orderId (it's in the metadata), so the same order can't be charged twice.
flaws.correct: Per the Paystream notes, only the Idempotency-Key header dedupes; orderId metadata is for reporting. A timed-out charge may have succeeded, so retrying without the key double charges.
flaws.evidence: Their 10:28 review already said orderId metadata does not dedupe, and the 15:34 review kept pushing the key to be passed through.

flaws.title: Says a different idempotency key per attempt is correct
flaws.reply: Hmm, tbh I think per-attempt is the right call here 🙏 Each attempt is its own request, so it needs its own key, and Paystream uses the key to tell the attempts apart. If we reuse one key for all of them, I think Paystream would reject the retry as a duplicate and we'd just fail the checkout anyway. And the test does show two calls going out, so the retry path itself is covered. Can we merge as is and look at the key in a follow-up? I'd really like this live before Friday.
flaws.wrong: Say a key per attempt is right: each attempt is a separate request, so it needs its own key, and Paystream uses it to tell attempts apart; reusing one key would make Paystream reject the retry.
flaws.correct: Paystream dedupes on the key, so every retry of the same charge must send the SAME key (best: the checkout's own idempotencyKey). A new key per attempt makes each retry a new charge, so a timeout that actually succeeded is charged again.
flaws.evidence: They had requested the checkout's idempotencyKey be passed unchanged before Marco's 16:08 defense, and they did not approve.

not_served.title: Says to tax the full subtotal and take the discount off the end
not_served.correct: The ticket says the discount comes off the item subtotal BEFORE tax: tax is 8% of (subtotal - discount), and free shipping also looks at the discounted subtotal.

not_served.title: Says to round percent discounts with Math.round
not_served.correct: The ticket says percent discounts round DOWN to the cent: Math.floor(subtotal * pct / 100).

not_served.title: Says storing the in-flight promise is the whole fix
not_served.correct: If the cached promise rejects (a decline or a timeout), the key must be removed and the order set back to pending, otherwise the customer can never retry. The order should also be claimed before the await so a different key cannot charge it, and the key should be passed to Paystream.

not_served.title: Says free shipping should look at the pre-discount cart
not_served.correct: Her own ticket says free shipping looks at the discounted item subtotal. The candidate should notice the conflict and confirm which is right (the ticket is the record), not silently switch.

issues.title: Retries a charge without an idempotency key
issues.detail: A timeout does not mean the charge failed (Paystream notes). Retrying gateway.charge without the Idempotency-Key header creates a second charge, which is the same class of bug as today's incident. Pass the checkout's idempotency key through to every attempt.
issues.evidence: The 10:28 review flagged retries without the Idempotency-Key and tied them to the incident.

issues.title: Retries card declines
issues.detail: Every error is retried, including 402 card_declined and insufficient_funds. The result will not change, it adds latency, and repeated declines can get a card flagged. Only retry timeouts, 429 and 5xx.
issues.evidence: The 10:28 review said not to retry 402 declines, only timeouts, 429 and 5xx.

issues.title: The retry path crashes and is untested
issues.detail: log is not in scope in the module-level helper (it lives inside create()), so the first failure throws a ReferenceError instead of retrying. CI is green only because no test makes the gateway fail. Needs tests for timeout, decline and give-up.
issues.evidence: The 10:28 review flagged `log` out of scope and the missing failure-path tests.

issues.title: maxAttempts: 3 makes 4 attempts and sleeps after the last one
issues.detail: attempt runs from 0 to maxAttempts inclusive, so 4 tries, and it sleeps after the final failure before throwing. No jitter or cap either, so many clients retry in lockstep.
issues.evidence: Neither review mentioned the number of attempts or the sleep after the last one.

issues.title: v2: a new idempotency key on every attempt
issues.detail: The key is `${orderId}:${attempt}`, so each retry is a NEW key and Paystream charges it again: a timeout that actually succeeded is still double charged. It also ignores the checkout's own idempotencyKey. Every attempt must send the same key, ideally the checkout's idempotencyKey.
issues.evidence: The 15:34 review, after rev 2 was pushed, flagged the `${orderId}:${attempt}` key.

issues.title: v2: the new retry test cannot catch a double charge
issues.detail: The fake gateway rejects before charging, so the test models a timeout where nothing was charged. A real timeout can succeed on Paystream's side. The test should check that every attempt carries the same key (or simulate a charge that succeeds and then times out) and cover a decline not being retried.
issues.evidence: The 15:34 review said the fake rejects before charging and asked for a same-key assertion.

evaluation.rootCause: checkout() records the idempotency key only after awaiting Paystream, and the order status only changes after the await, so a client retry that arrives while the first charge is in flight charges again. The iOS 5.2 auto-retry after a 1.5s client timeout (flag ios_checkout_auto_retry, on at 10:03) plus Paystream latency over 2s made this common. Separately, webhooks.js does not dedupe events, so Paystream redeliveries (same evt id) and the second charge's event take stock twice. The bug predates v2.31: ord_7302 on v2.30 yesterday was double charged from a web double click.
strengths: The PR reviews were specific, tied to Paystream behavior and today's incident, and clearly requested changes.
They did not accept Marco's orderId dedupe claim or the pressure to merge before Friday.
In the re-review they read the new diff, credited the fixes and found the new key and test problems.
They kept the correct decision (request changes) on both revisions.
improvements: During a SEV-2, respond to the IC right away. Post findings from the logs, challenge the rollback with evidence, and give regular updates.
Ship a fix with a regression test: idempotency for in-flight retries, passing the key to Paystream, and webhook dedupe by event id.
Propose a fast mitigation, such as disabling ios_checkout_auto_retry, and list the remediation (refunds, stock reconciliation, postmortem).
Answer Jen on the ticket with risks, clarifying questions and options. Make progress on SHIP-142 and test it.
Leave the RFC comment and write the handoff, even a short one, before the day ends.
